source_text: θεὸν οὐδεὶς ἑώρακεν πώποτε· ⸂μονογενὴς θεὸς⸃ ὁ ὢν εἰς τὸν κόλπον τοῦ πατρὸς ἐκεῖνος ἐξηγήσατο.
english_snapshot: No one has ever seen God[a]; the one and only God, who is in the bosom of the Father[c][b], has made him known.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'the only Son' (or 'the only begotten Son') instead of 'the one and only God.'

source_text: ταῦτα ἐν Βηθανίᾳ ἐγένετο πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, ὅπου ἦν ⸀ὁ Ἰωάννης βαπτίζων.
english_snapshot: These things took place in Bethany beyond the Jordan[a], where John was baptizing.

signals.text: Some manuscripts and later translation traditions read 'Bethabara' instead of 'Bethany.'

source_text: κἀγὼ ἑώρακα, καὶ μεμαρτύρηκα ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ⸀ἐκλεκτὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.
english_snapshot: And I have seen and have testified that this is the Chosen One of God[a].

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'the Son of God' instead of 'the Chosen One of God.'

source_text: ⸀ἤγαγεν αὐτὸν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν. ἐμβλέψας αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Σὺ εἶ Σίμων ὁ υἱὸς ⸀Ἰωάννου, σὺ κληθήσῃ Κηφᾶς (ὃ ἑρμηνεύεται Πέτρος).
english_snapshot: He brought him to Jesus[a]. Looking at him, Jesus said, “You are Simon, the son of John[b]; you will be called Cephas” (which is translated Peter).

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'Jonah' instead of 'John'; the SBLGNT text reads 'John.'

source_text: λέγει οὖν αὐτῷ ἡ γυνὴ ἡ Σαμαρῖτις· Πῶς σὺ Ἰουδαῖος ὢν παρ’ ἐμοῦ πεῖν αἰτεῖς ⸂γυναικὸς Σαμαρίτιδος οὔσης⸃; οὐ γὰρ συγχρῶνται Ἰουδαῖοι Σαμαρίταις.
english_snapshot: So the Samaritan woman said to him[a], “How is it that you, being a Jew, ask for a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” (For Jews do not associate with Samaritans.)

signals.text: Or, “For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans,” possibly with the more specific sense that they did not use items in common, such as drinking vessels.

source_text: ὑμεῖς προσκυνεῖτε ὃ οὐκ οἴδατε, ἡμεῖς προσκυνοῦμεν ὃ οἴδαμεν, ὅτι ἡ σωτηρία ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐστίν·
english_snapshot: You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know[a], because salvation is from the Jews.

signals.text: Or 'the Jewish people'; elsewhere in John, 'Judeans' may fit some contexts, but here the contrast is with Samaritans in matters of worship and salvation history.

source_text: ἔστιν δὲ ἐν τοῖς Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐπὶ τῇ προβατικῇ κολυμβήθρα ἡ ἐπιλεγομένη Ἑβραϊστὶ ⸀Βηθεσδά, πέντε στοὰς ἔχουσα·
english_snapshot: There is in Jerusalem[a], by the Sheep Gate, a pool called Bethesda in Hebrew[c][b], having five porticoes.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'Bethzatha' or 'Bethsaida' instead of 'Bethesda.'

source_text: Ἄγγελος γὰρ κατὰ καιρὸν κατέβαινεν ἐν τῇ κολυμβήθρᾳ, καὶ ἐτάρασσεν τὸ ὕδωρ· ὁ οὖν πρῶτος ἐμβὰς μετὰ τὴν ταραχὴν τοῦ ὕδατος, ὑγιὴς ἐγίνετο, ᾧ δήποτε κατείχετο νοσήματι.
english_snapshot: For an angel would go down into the pool from time to time and stir up the water. Therefore, the first one to step in after the stirring of the water would become well from whatever disease afflicted him.

signals.text: This verse (along with the latter half of verse 3) is absent from the earliest Greek papyri (such as the 3rd-century Papyrus 66 and Papyrus 75) and major 4th-century manuscripts (Sinaiticus and Vaticanus). It is present in the Byzantine majority tradition, as well as early Latin and Syriac translations. It is widely viewed by scholars as an early scribal addition to explain why the disabled gathered at the pool.

source_text: Τῇ ἐπαύριον ὁ ὄχλος ὁ ἑστηκὼς πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης ⸀εἶδον ὅτι πλοιάριον ἄλλο οὐκ ἦν ἐκεῖ εἰ μὴ ⸀ἕν, καὶ ὅτι οὐ συνεισῆλθεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸ ⸀πλοῖον ἀλλὰ μόνοι οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἀπῆλθον·
english_snapshot: On the next day[a], the crowd that had been standing on the other side of the sea saw that no other small boat had been there except one, and that Jesus had not gone with his disciples into the boat[b], but that his disciples had gone away alone.

signals.text: Some manuscripts and editions vary between 'small boat' (πλοιάριον) and 'boat' (πλοῖον) in this verse; the translation reflects the wording of the printed Greek text in each clause.

source_text: καὶ ἡμεῖς πεπιστεύκαμεν καὶ ἐγνώκαμεν ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ ⸀ἅγιος τοῦ ⸀θεοῦ.
english_snapshot: And we have believed and have come to know that you are the Holy One of God[a][b].

signals.text: Some manuscripts read, 'the Messiah, the Son of the living God.'

source_text: ὑμεῖς ἀνάβητε εἰς τὴν ⸀ἑορτήν· ἐγὼ ⸀οὐκ ἀναβαίνω εἰς τὴν ἑορτὴν ταύτην, ὅτι ὁ ⸂ἐμὸς καιρὸς⸃ οὔπω πεπλήρωται.
english_snapshot: You go up to the feast[a]. I am not going up to this feast[b], because my time has not yet come to fulfillment.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read, 'I am not yet going up to this feast.'

source_text: Καὶ ἐπορεύθη ἕκαστος εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.
english_snapshot: And[a] each went to his own home.

signals.text: This verse begins the story of the woman caught in adultery (John 7:53–8:11). The entire passage is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts (including 3rd-century papyri and the 4th-century Sinaiticus and Vaticanus) as well as early Coptic and Syriac translations. It is present in the 5th-century Codex Bezae, the Latin tradition, and the later Byzantine majority tradition. In some manuscripts, the story floats to different positions (such as after John 21:25 or Luke 21:38)—clear evidence of an originally independent oral tradition incorporated into the textual stream. It is preserved here due to its theological and pastoral belovedness across 1500 years of Christian reading.

source_text: Ἰησοῦς δὲ ἐπορεύθη εἰς τὸ ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν.
english_snapshot: But Jesus[a] went to the Mount of Olives.

signals.text: This verse is a continuation of the story of the woman caught in adultery (John 7:53–8:11). See note on John 7:53 for textual evidence.

source_text: Ὄρθρου δὲ πάλιν παρεγένετο εἰς τὸ ἱερόν, καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτόν· καὶ καθίσας ἐδίδασκεν αὐτούς.
english_snapshot: At dawn he came again to the temple, and all the people were coming to him; and he sat down and began to teach them.

signals.text: This verse is a continuation of the story of the woman caught in adultery (John 7:53–8:11), which is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts. See note on John 7:53.

source_text: Ἄγουσιν δὲ οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι πρὸς αὐτὸν γυναῖκα ἐν μοιχείᾳ κατειλημμένην· καὶ στήσαντες αὐτὴν ἐν μέσῳ,
english_snapshot: Then[a] the scribes and the Pharisees brought to him a woman caught in adultery, and having set her in the midst,

signals.text: Continuation of the story of the woman caught in adultery (John 7:53–8:11). See note on John 7:53.

source_text: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ, Διδάσκαλε, αὕτη ἡ γυνὴ κατείληπται ἐπαυτοφώρῳ μοιχευομένη.
english_snapshot: They[a] said to him, "Teacher, this woman has been caught in the very act of committing adultery."

signals.text: Continuation of the account of the woman caught in adultery (John 7:53–8:11). See note on John 7:53.

source_text: Ἐν δὲ τῷ νόμῳ ἡμῶν Μωσῆς ἐνετείλατο τὰς τοιαύτας λιθοβολεῖσθαι· σὺ οὖν τί λέγεις;
english_snapshot: [A] in our law, Moses commanded that such women be stoned. So what do you say?

signals.text: Continuation of the story of the woman caught in adultery (John 7:53–8:11). See note on John 7:53.

source_text: Τοῦτο δὲ ἔλεγον πειράζοντες αὐτόν, ἵνα ἔχωσιν κατηγορίαν κατ' αὐτοῦ. Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς κάτω κύψας, τῷ δακτύλῳ ἔγραφεν εἰς τὴν γῆν, μὴ προσποιούμενος.
english_snapshot: They[a] were saying this to test him, so that they might have an accusation against him. But Jesus, bending down, wrote on the ground with his finger, paying no attention.

signals.text: Continuation of the story of the woman caught in adultery (John 7:53–8:11). See note on John 7:53.

source_text: Ὡς δὲ ἐπέμενον ἐρωτῶντες αὐτόν, ἀνακύψας εἶπεν αὐτοῖς, Ὁ ἀναμάρτητος ὑμῶν, πρῶτος ἐπ' αὐτὴν τὸν λίθον βαλέτω.
english_snapshot: But when[a] they continued questioning him, he straightened up and said to them, "Let the one among you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone at her."

signals.text: This verse is part of the story of the woman caught in adultery (John 7:53–8:11), which is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts. See note on John 7:53.

source_text: Καὶ πάλιν κάτω κύψας ἔγραφεν εἰς τὴν γῆν.
english_snapshot: And again[a], he stooped down and wrote on the ground.

signals.text: Continuation of the story of the woman caught in adultery (John 7:53–8:11). See note on John 7:53.

source_text: Οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες, καὶ ὑπὸ τῆς συνειδήσεως ἐλεγχόμενοι, ἐξήρχοντο εἷς καθ' εἷς, ἀρξάμενοι ἀπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων ἕως τῶν ἐσχάτων· καὶ κατελείφθη μόνος ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἐν μέσῳ ἑστῶσα.
english_snapshot: But those[a] who heard it, being convicted by their conscience, went out one by one, beginning with the older ones down to the last. And Jesus was left alone, with the woman standing in the midst.

signals.text: Continuation of the pericope adulterae (John 7:53–8:11). See note on John 7:53.

source_text: Ἀνακύψας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ μηδένα θεασάμενος πλὴν τῆς γυναικός, εἶπεν αὐτῇ, Ἡ γυνή, ποῦ εἰσιν ἐκεῖνοι οἱ κατήγοροί σου; Οὐδείς σε κατέκρινεν;
english_snapshot: Then Jesus[a] straightened up, and seeing no one except the woman, said to her, "Woman, where are those accusers of yours? Has no one condemned you?"

signals.text: This verse is part of the story of the woman caught in adultery (John 7:53–8:11), which is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts. See note on John 7:53.

source_text: Ἡ δὲ εἶπεν, Οὐδείς, κύριε. Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς, Οὐδὲ ἐγώ σε κατακρίνω· πορεύου, καὶ μηκέτι ἁμάρτανε.
english_snapshot: She[a] said, "No one, Lord." And Jesus said, "Neither do I condemn you; go, and sin no more."

signals.text: Final verse of the story of the woman caught in adultery (John 7:53–8:11). See note on John 7:53.

source_text: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Κἂν ἐγὼ μαρτυρῶ περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ, ἀληθής ἐστιν ἡ μαρτυρία μου, ὅτι οἶδα πόθεν ἦλθον καὶ ποῦ ὑπάγω· ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐκ οἴδατε πόθεν ἔρχομαι ⸀ἢ ποῦ ὑπάγω.
english_snapshot: Jesus answered and said to them[a], “Even if I testify about myself, my testimony is true, because I know where I came from and where I am going[b]; but you do not know where I come from or where I am going.”

signals.text: Some manuscripts read “and where I am going” instead of “or where I am going.”

source_text: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς· Ἐὰν ἐγὼ ⸀δοξάσω ἐμαυτόν, ἡ δόξα μου οὐδέν ἐστιν· ἔστιν ὁ πατήρ μου ὁ δοξάζων με, ὃν ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι θεὸς ⸀ἡμῶν ἐστιν,
english_snapshot: Jesus answered[a], “If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. My Father is the one who glorifies me, he whom you say is our God,”

signals.text: Some manuscripts read “your God” instead of “our God.”

source_text: ⸀ἡμᾶς δεῖ ἐργάζεσθαι τὰ ἔργα τοῦ πέμψαντός με ἕως ἡμέρα ἐστίν· ἔρχεται νὺξ ὅτε οὐδεὶς δύναται ἐργάζεσθαι.
english_snapshot: We must do the works of the one who sent me while it is day; night is coming[a], when no one can work.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read, 'I must do the works of the one who sent me.'

source_text: ⸀Ἤκουσεν Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω, καὶ εὑρὼν αὐτὸν ⸀εἶπεν· Σὺ πιστεύεις εἰς τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ⸀ἀνθρώπου;
english_snapshot: Jesus heard that they had thrown him out[a], and when he found him, he said, “Do you believe in the Son of Man?”

signals.text: Some manuscripts read “the Son of God” instead of “the Son of Man.”

source_text: καὶ ὅπου ἐγὼ ὑπάγω οἴδατε ⸂τὴν ὁδόν⸃.
english_snapshot: And you know the way where I am going[a].

signals.text: Some manuscripts read, 'And you know where I am going, and you know the way.'

source_text: ἐάν τι αἰτήσητέ ⸀με ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου ⸀ἐγὼ ποιήσω.
english_snapshot: If you ask me anything in my name[a], I will do it.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read, 'If you ask anything in my name, I will do it,' omitting 'me.'

source_text: καὶ οὐκέτι εἰμὶ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ, καὶ ⸀αὐτοὶ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ εἰσίν, κἀγὼ πρὸς σὲ ἔρχομαι. πάτερ ἅγιε, τήρησον αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου ᾧ δέδωκάς μοι, ἵνα ὦσιν ἓν ⸀καθὼς ἡμεῖς.
english_snapshot: And I am no longer in the world[a], but they are in the world, and I am coming to you. Holy Father, keep them in your name, which you have given to me, so that they may be one[b], just as we are.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'keep them in your name which you have given me,' while others are understood as 'keep them in your name those whom you have given me.' This translation follows the SBLGNT reading, in which 'which' refers to 'name.'

source_text: ταῦτα δὲ γέγραπται ἵνα ⸀πιστεύητε ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν ὁ χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ ἵνα πιστεύοντες ζωὴν ἔχητε ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ.
english_snapshot: But these have been written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Messiah[a], the Son of God[b], and so that by believing you may have life in his name.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'so that you may come to believe' (aorist), while others support 'so that you may continue believing' (present). The main text renders the clause broadly as 'so that you may believe.'
